done.why: Every way forward I found was blocked by rockfalls or a crumbling ledge, and the well etchings gave me nothing to act on.

about: An underground cave system in the Zork tradition. It has a barrow, a cavern with a ravine, a disorienting carousel room, a riddle door, a well room, a formal garden, and a wizard who flits through. Much of it is walled off for later.

ending.what: No ending. I stopped at the Deep Ford, where the ledge north won't hold me yet.

moments.note: The Carousel Room scrambles directions and dropped me into the Riddle Room.
Answering 'well' made the stone door swing open.
The etchings are broken letters I could not turn into a word.
The bucket would not go up or down, and 'exit' was not understood.
Rockfalls blocked the carousel exits, so there is little to pursue.
The wizard appeared and muttered, then vanished.
The ledge crumbled, so I was turned back at the edge of the explorable area.

wished: Work out the etchings in the well room, or a way to use the bucket
Get past the ledge at the Deep Ford
Find out what the gazebo is for

lines.line: There is a deafening clap of thunder and the stone door quietly swings open to reveal a passageway beyond.
lines.why: The one clear puzzle I solved.

lines.line: You start up toward the ledge, and the rock comes away in your hand. Whatever is along there will keep until you are better equipped for it.
lines.why: Told me the way on exists but I am not ready for it.

fun.why: Familiar and pleasant, but short, and the exits ran out quickly.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal at first, but it dried up at the blocked exits.

difficulty.why: The riddle was easy. The etchings and the bucket gave me no clear next step.

interestingness.why: Classic locations with a few small surprises.

prose.why: The descriptions were concise and atmospheric, and the blocked-way messages were charming.
